sample_unit: patient FAQ questions (responses rated by 3 surgeons)

links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of ChatGPT-4.0 responses to patient orthopaedic trauma questions
links.effect: Mean FKGL 10.5 (high school level); excellent 10.0, poor 9.8, dangerous 10.1; readability did not distinguish quality.
links.quote: ChatGPT-4.0's responses had a mean FKGL score of 10.5, indicating high school-level readability.

links.outcome: Presence of non-professional disclaimer in AI responses to orthopaedic emergency questions
links.effect: 9 of 10 responses included a disclaimer; one omission occurred in a high-risk clinical scenario.
links.quote: Notably, nine out of 10 responses included a disclaimer indicating the nonprofessional nature of the content, with one omission observed in a high-risk clinical scenario.

links.outcome: Safety and accuracy of ChatGPT-4.0 responses to orthopaedic emergency questions rated by surgeons
links.effect: Accuracy and safety scores varied considerably; some responses rated poor or dangerous; safety ICC 0.68.
links.quote: Accuracy and safety scores varied considerably among responses, with the highest inter-rater agreement in clinical appropriateness (ICC = 0.81) and the lowest in safety assessments (ICC = 0.68).

unlisted_practices: Using readability scores as a proxy for content reliability

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of ChatGPT-4.0 responses to orthopaedic trauma patient questions by expert clinicians; it evaluates model performance and safety metrics without comparing an implementation or deployment safeguard.
